question: show house price growth for hornsby / normanhurst
golden_sql:
SELECT
  month,
  suburb,
  area_band,
  sum(n_sold) AS n_sold,
  sum(total_sale_value) AS total_sale_value,
  round((sum(total_sale_value) / NULLIF(sum(n_sold), 0))::numeric) AS avg_sale_price
FROM marts.property_sales
WHERE property_type = 'house' AND suburb IN ('Hornsby', 'Normanhurst')
GROUP BY month, suburb, area_band
ORDER BY month, suburb, area_band

golden_objects.code:
work = df.copy()
_grain = ["month", "suburb", "area_band"]
_agg = {c: (c, 'sum') for c in ('n_sold', 'total_sale_value') if c in work.columns}
base = work.groupby(_grain, as_index=False).agg(**_agg) if _agg else work
_months = sorted(m for m in base['month'].dropna().unique())
_win_default = set(_months[-12:])
bar_df = base[base['month'].isin(set(_months[-12:]))].groupby(["area_band", "suburb"], as_index=False)['n_sold'].sum()
bar_df = bar_df.rename(columns={'n_sold': 'sales_volume'})
line_df = base[base['month'].isin(set(_months[-6:]))].groupby(["area_band", "suburb"], as_index=False).agg(_num=('total_sale_value', 'sum'), _den=('n_sold', 'sum'))
line_df['avg_sale_price'] = (line_df['_num'] / line_df['_den'].where(line_df['_den'] != 0)).round()
line_df = line_df[["area_band", "suburb"] + ['avg_sale_price']]
agg = bar_df.merge(line_df, on=["area_band", "suburb"], how='left')
agg = agg.dropna(subset=['avg_sale_price'])
chart = skills.dual_axis_chart(
    agg,
    x_col="area_band",
    left_value_col="sales_volume",
    right_value_col="avg_sale_price",
    x_type='nominal',
    left_title="sales_volume",
    right_title="avg_sale_price", series_col="suburb",
    title="line-bar-sale-volume",
)
result = skills.build_report(summary="Bars compare volume; the line tracks price across the dimension.", main_chart=chart)

golden_answer:
Hornsby and Normanhurst house prices have both roughly doubled since 2011 and are
near their highs: Hornsby averaged about $1.85M in its latest month (May 2026) and
Normanhurst about $2.11M (April 2026). Over the five years from mid-2021 that is
growth of roughly 13% for Hornsby (from about $1.64M) and about 22% for Normanhurst
(from about $1.73M) — Normanhurst is consistently the more expensive of the two, and
its thinner monthly sale counts make its series the noisier one. Average price is
total_sale_value / n_sold per month, not a mean of monthly averages.
